title: Animals: A Tour of the Kingdoms

cards.h: A family of over a million
cards.b: About 1.3 to 1.5 million animal species have been named, and most are insects. Knowing the main groups, and how each is built, shows how body plans evolved and why habitats matter for conservation.

Animals are multicellular eukaryotes that eat other organisms, have no cell walls, and most can move at some stage. They are grouped by body plan: symmetry, body layers, a body cavity, segmentation and a backbone.

• Porifera (sponges): pores, no true tissues.
  • Cnidaria: jellyfish, coral, stinging cells.
  • Platyhelminthes: flatworms, tapeworm.
  • Nematoda: roundworms.
  • Annelida: segmented worms like earthworms.
  • Mollusca: snails, octopus, soft body.
  • Arthropoda: insects, spiders, crabs. Jointed legs and a chitin shell. The largest phylum.
  • Echinodermata: starfish, spiny skin.
All belong to phylum Chordata. Five classes:

At some stage, all chordates have a notochord, a hollow nerve cord above it, and gill slits. In vertebrates the notochord becomes the backbone. Warm-blooded animals (birds, mammals) keep a steady body temperature using energy; cold-blooded ones rely on the environment.

Insects have three body parts, six legs and often wings. Many go through metamorphosis (egg, larva, pupa, adult in butterflies). Bees, ants and termites live in complex societies. Karl von Frisch decoded the honeybee waggle dance (Nobel 1973).
Egg-laying mammals (monotremes: platypus), pouched mammals (marsupials: kangaroo) and placental mammals (most). Whales and bats show how a mammal can return to water or learn to fly.
Linnaeus (1758) set the base. Cuvier grouped animals by body plan (1812). Today DNA sequences revise trees: for example, birds are living dinosaurs, and whales are close kin to hippos.

Fix these

  • Spiders are not insects (eight legs, two body parts).
  • Whales and bats are mammals, not fish or birds.
  • A jellyfish or starfish is not a fish.

India shelters tiger, Asian elephant, Asiatic lion (only in Gir, Gujarat), one-horned rhinoceros and the gharial. Project Tiger began in 1973 and India now has more than 3,000 tigers by the 2022 count (3,682 estimated). Project Cheetah (2022) reintroduced cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa. Salim Ali (1896-1987), the Birdman of India, wrote the Book of Indian Birds (1941). The Wildlife (Protection) Act of 1972 protects species.

• Animals are grouped by body plan.
  • Arthropods are the largest phylum.
  • Five vertebrate classes: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals.
  • Many species exist only in India's special habitats.
